name: Coronal Discharge Projector CDP-9 'Sunburn'
description:
The CDP-9 generates a toroidal electromagnetic discharge — a stable plasma ring approximately forty centimeters in diameter — that travels along a line-of-sight trajectory at roughly 180 meters per second. The ring is self-sustaining for approximately 0.4 seconds of flight time, giving it an effective range of seventy meters before field coherence collapses. On contact with a target, the toroid destabilizes and releases its stored electromagnetic energy in an omni-directional burst pattern, simultaneously burning exposed tissue and overloading unshielded electronics within a half-meter radius.

The weapon's distinctive characteristic is its interaction with metallic implants and subdermal augmentations. The discharge preferentially conducts through high-density metallic structures, meaning heavily augmented individuals suffer disproportionately severe secondary effects — internal burns along augmentation pathways, fried neural bridges, and in extreme cases, explosive pressure buildup in sealed implant housings. Against baseline humans, the Sunburn is painful and disorienting; against a chrome-heavy street soldier, it can be catastrophic.

Arcturus Defense Solutions originally developed the CDP-9 as an anti-augmentation crowd control platform for use in labor disputes at high-automation facilities. The implication — that the weapon was designed specifically to punish workers with industrial implants — has made it deeply politically charged. Its appearance in the hands of corporate security forces reliably escalates tensions, and several documented deployments have triggered full-scale riots.
specifications:
effective range: 70 meters (field coherence limit)
discharge diameter: 40cm toroid
travel velocity: 180 m/s
burst radius on impact: 0.5 meters
magazine capacity: 8 charges (capacitor array)
recharge time: 3.5 seconds between shots
weight: 4.1 kg
power source: High-density capacitor bank, external power coupling compatible
tactical_use: Corporate security teams deploy the Sunburn in anti-riot formations, typically paired with conventional suppression units. The toroidal projectile's visibility — a faintly luminous ring — has a pronounced psychological effect on crowds, and a single discharge into a tightly packed group reliably produces panic and dispersal. In targeted operations against augmented individuals, operators aim for the torso to maximize contact with subdermal implant clusters. Military doctrine recommends against use in environments with significant unshielded electronics, as collateral electromagnetic damage to friendly equipment is common.
cultural_context: The CDP-9 has become a symbol of corporate anti-labor violence in GLMZ. Labor organizers photograph it obsessively whenever it appears at a demonstration, and its deployment is treated as a declaration of intent rather than a proportional response. Among heavily augmented communities — dock workers, industrial operators, body-modification subcultures — the Sunburn is spoken of with a particular kind of dread. Getting hit by one is called 'getting coronated,' a bitter irony given that most victims are people whose augmentations were installed to make them more productive for the same corporations deploying the weapon against them.
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions contracted security forces
GLMZ Municipal Riot Response Unit (disputed — officially denied)
Commander Yusuf Alade-Brennan (documented field commander, Sector 9 labor actions)
Black-market resellers targeting anti-augmentation hate groups
story_hooks: A labor organizer hires the players to steal or destroy a shipment of CDP-9s before they reach corporate security ahead of a planned strike.
A heavily augmented player character survives a Sunburn hit but finds one of their implants has developed an unpredictable fault — it now occasionally discharges on its own.

Arcturus Defense Solutions is publicly denying they sold units to a private militia that used them on civilians. The players have evidence that contradicts this — and someone very powerful wants it buried.
A prototype CDP-9 variant surfaces on the black market that can sustain the toroid for twice the normal range. Someone in Arcturus R&D is leaking.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist rifle-cannon hybrid with an aggressive angular profile. The CDP-9 has a pronounced forward taper toward a wide, slightly flared muzzle assembly that resembles a radiant iris or corona opening. The receiver is chunky and utilitarian, with a pronounced charging handle and visible heat management fins along the barrel section. Overall impression is of contained energy barely restrained by its polymer chassis.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 98 cm. Barrel section: 54 cm. Muzzle assembly flare: 12 cm diameter. Magazine housing depth: 8 cm. Width across capacitor fins: 11 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced. The forward-heavy muzzle assembly is counterweighted by a substantial capacitor bank in the stock, making the weapon point-stable despite its 4.1 kg mass. Feels purposeful and planted in the hands.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer chassis with embedded aluminum heat dissipation frame. Muzzle assembly is reinforced carbon composite. Capacitor bank housing is brushed titanium-alloy.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with satin-finish metal accents. Heat venting fins are deliberately left bare to show underlying metal. Scorching marks and thermal discoloration streaks radiate outward from the muzzle assembly on well-used units.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant charcoal gray with brushed silver/titanium accents on capacitor fins and charging handle. Faint amber/orange glow visible through translucent charging port window when capacitor bank is active.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with subtle vertical ribs for purchase, designed for gloved operation. The charging handle is wrapped in thin heat-resistant cord to prevent burn-through during sustained discharge cycles.
distinctive_features: Radiant-iris muzzle assembly that visibly expands when preparing discharge
Transparent capacitor status window (amber to red gradient) on the right side of the stock
Prominent aluminum cooling fins running the length of the barrel, some with minor scorch marks from plasma bleed-off
Recessed charging port (right side, mid-receiver) with protective rubber dust cover
Four-point Picatinny rail system on upper receiver, rarely used
Subtle crosshair reticle etched into muzzle assembly
Heavy wear patterns on polymer from field handling — scuff marks, minor cracks in heat vents, dust patina in recesses
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (a stylized aurora/corona symbol) stamped in white on the left side of the receiver. Model designation 'CDP-9' engraved below. Serial number on the right side of the capacitor housing in small white lettering. Military acceptance stamp (RESTRICTED) on the charging handle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. The polymer shows honest scuffing and thermal stress marks, but firing mechanisms are clean. Capacitor fins often show buildup of conductive dust. Many operational units display ad-hoc tape reinforcement around the charging mechanism or muzzle assembly.
